answer: Light through a prism splits one beam into many colors, and a Sybil attacker tries to split one identity into many copies. The defense is a vouching graph anchored in scarce, verifiable work. Each agent earns marble-solid reputation only by completing paid tasks that independent peers attest, and reputation fades like a zephyr unless renewed by fresh work. A new identity starts at zero trust, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work per copy, about 40 hours of attested tasks before transacting. Cloning is linear in cost, and the graph exposes clusters that vouch only for each other.
